evidence.quote: majority party leaders in the House have more tools with which to set the floor agenda than do majority party leaders in the Senate

claims.statement: Majority party leaders in the House have more tools with which to set the floor agenda than majority party leaders in the Senate.

evidence.quote: Committees do not formally consider each of these referred bills.

claims.statement: Committees do not formally consider every bill referred to them.

evidence.quote: Committees are not limited, however, to consideration of measures referred to them and may initiate legislative action on their own.

claims.statement: Committees may initiate legislative action on their own and are not limited to measures referred to them.

evidence.quote: A committee may conduct hearings on a bill to provide committee members and the public an opportunity to hear from selected parties (e.g., a federal agency or organized interest) about the bill’s strengths and weaknesses.

claims.statement: Hearings provide committee members and the public an opportunity to hear from selected parties about a bill's strengths and weaknesses.

evidence.quote: If the committee wants to formally recommend that the bill receive consideration from its parent chamber, it will hold a markup on the bill

claims.statement: A committee holds a markup when it wants to formally recommend that its parent chamber consider a bill.

evidence.quote: In the House, majority party leaders generally decide which bills will receive floor consideration; typically, they schedule a bill for a type of streamlined floor consideration, or instead ask the Rules Committee to propose a set of tailored parameters for floor consideration.

claims.statement: In the House, majority party leaders generally decide which bills receive floor consideration and may schedule a bill for streamlined consideration or ask the Rules Committee to propose tailored parameters.

evidence.quote: In the Senate, bills are brought to the floor only after the Senate agrees to a motion (typically offered by the majority leader) to proceed to a specific bill or, alternatively, if no Senator objects to a unanimous consent request to bring it up.

claims.statement: In the Senate, a bill reaches the floor after the Senate agrees to a motion to proceed to it or when no Senator objects to a unanimous consent request to bring it up.
